paper.title_en: Dephasing-Induced Universal Spin Fluctuations in a Localized Hubbard Chain
paper.abstract_en: Decoherence usually washes out quantum effects. We show that in a disordered chain it can instead switch on universal fluctuations. In the infinite-$U$ Hubbard chain, particles cannot pass one another, so the spin crossing a cut is fixed by the number of particles that cross. Without an environment, disorder localizes the charge and the spin fluctuations stop growing. Dephasing restores diffusion: the spin width grows again as $t^{1/8}$, fastest at an intermediate dephasing rate, and the spin distribution takes the same non-Gaussian M-Wright form as in the clean chain.
